Certainly. Below is a structured 12-week strength program for a 36-year-old recreational lifter recovering from a right medial meniscus tear. The plan emphasizes low-impact strength with controlled knee loading, avoids jumping and deep knee flexion under load, and progresses toward ski readiness. It uses a full gym and targets improved lower-body strength, stability, mobility, and overall conditioning to support a safe return to skiing. Each week includes 3–4 days of resistance training plus optional cardio and recovery work. If any exercise causes knee pain beyond mild discomfort, stop it and switch to a safer alternative.

Assumptions and guidelines
- Training age: recreational lifter, 6 months post-injury, surgeon’s clearance for low-impact strength only.
- Pain: No sharp pain, swelling, or mechanical symptoms with any exercise. Stop if pain worsens.
- Conditioning: 2–3 days of cardio recommended (low-impact options). Mobility work daily.
- Progression: Load progression by 2–5% each week for upper-limb and hip-dominant exercises when form is solid and no pain. For knee-dominant or loaded knee flexion movements, progress more conservatively.

Phases overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundations, control, and tissue-friendly loading. Build confidence with movement quality, establish baseline strength, re-tune knee flexion mechanics.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–8): Strength-building with controlled knee loading. Introduce more workload on hips, glutes, quads with safe ranges. Begin moderate leg press, leg extension variations, isometrics, and hip-dedicated work.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength and preparation for skiing demands. Increase total training stress with higher loads, tempo work, and functional carryover for knee stabilization and lower-body power without impact.

Weekly structure
- 4 training days per week (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) recommended. If schedule requires 3 days, keep days non-consecutive (e.g., Mon-Wed-Sat) and drop optional sessions.
- 2 optional cardio/conditioning days (light swims, cycling on low resistance, brisk walk, or elliptical) on non-lift days or after sessions.
- 10–15 minutes of warm-up before each session (user-controlled mobility and activation). 5–10 minutes of cool-down.

Equipment used
- Barbell, EZ-bar or dumbbells
- Power rack or safety supports
- Leg extension and leg curl machines (adjusted to safe ranges)
- Leg press machine
- Hip thrust / glute bridge setup
- Cable station / resistance bands
- Adjustable bench
- Step platform with height options
- Stability ball, foam roller, lacrosse ball for mobility

Important exercise notes
- Depth and ROM: For knee-friendly work, avoid deep knee flexion under load. For example, squat variants should stay above parallel or be performed with partial range and elevated heel to reduce knee flexion load. Leg press depth should be controlled to mid-range; leg extensions should be performed with light to moderate load and not near the extreme ROM.
- Tempo: Use a controlled tempo (3–1–1–0 or 2–0–2–0 depending on exercise) to maximize time under tension without jolting joints.
- Symmetry: Prioritize balanced loading between both legs; use single-leg work to address asymmetries but keep loads conservative.
- Pain monitoring: If swelling increases or joint pain worsens, reduce load or revert to prior week’s level.

Goal: Establish form, tissue tolerance, and knee-friendly strength base.

Week 12
- Peak week to test readiness

- Lighter accessory work to maintain movement quality: Glute bridge variations, leg curls, abductor/adductor 2x12-15
- Conditioning finisher: 15–20 minutes of low-impact rowing or cycling at moderate intensity, ensuring knee comfort
- Mobility and flexibility focus to wrap up: 10–15 minutes

Conditioning and conditioning progression
- Week 1–3: 2–3 days of 15–25 minutes low-impact cardio (elliptical, cycling) at easy to moderate effort.
- Week 4–6: Increase cardio to 20–30 minutes; include one day of strides or light tempo efforts if knee tolerance allows.
- Week 7–12: Maintain 20–40 minutes, with one longer session weekly (30–40 minutes) at low-to-moderate intensity; consider ski-specific conditioning (on-snow simulators, roller ski if available) only if cleared and no pain.

Mobility and injury prevention
- Daily knee-friendly mobility: ankle dorsiflexion, knee flexion control, hip ROM, IT band release with foam roller.
- Hip stability: clamshells, side-lying leg lifts, monster walks with mini-band.
- Core stability: anti-rotation, dead bugs, farmer carries.
- Balance/proprioception: single-leg stance on stable surface then progress to unstable (BOSU or foam pad) as tolerated with no pain.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Protein target: 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day to support recovery and adaptation.
- Caloric intake: maintain or modestly surplus if aiming to gain strength; avoid excessive weight gain that could increase knee joint load.
- Hydration: 2–3 liters per day, adjust for body size and activity level.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours per night, consistent schedule.
- Post-workout nutrition: 20–40 g protein and 20–40 g carbohydrates within 1–2 hours after workouts to support recovery.
- Anti-inflammatory strategies: Use icing or cold therapy if swelling occurs after workouts; gentle active recovery on off days.

- Reassess every 3 weeks for form and progression readiness.

- Weights should stay challenging but controlled. When form or pain changes, reduce weight, not ROM.

Return-to-ski considerations
- Ensure comfortable knee ROM with controlled, loaded movements at all speeds; no impact landings.
- Build endurance for ski-season demands with controlled steps and simulated pivoting and edging motions that do not load the knee excessively.
- Gradually reintroduce plyometric or dynamic loading only after clearance and with sport-specific progressions (e.g., skate jumps, bounding) if clinically cleared.

Daily warm-up (before training, 5–10 minutes)

- Thoracic mobility: 1–2 minutes of thoracic foam rolling or banded thoracic rotations (limit neck strain).

Mobility progression plan (weeks 1–12)
- Ankle dorsiflexion: wall ankle mobilizations, 2 sets of 12–15 reps per ankle; progress to can-do deep squat position with gentle pokes into ROM.
- Hip internal/external rotation: 2–3 sets of 12–15 reps per side; use couch stretch for hip flexors as needed.
- Hip flexor/quad length: couch stretch 2–3 sets of 30–60 seconds per side.
- Hamstrings: seated or standing hamstring stretch 2–3 sets of 30 seconds per leg; add Nordic hamstring–friendly eccentrics if tolerated later.
- Glutes and adductors: 2–3 sets of 12–15 reps of clamshells, side-lying leg lifts, 90/90 hip mobility, and adductor squeezes with a light ball between knees.
- Thoracic spine: thoracic rotations 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps per side; seated thoracic extension against a wall (or foam roller) for 30–60 seconds.
- Calves: gastrocnemius and soleus stretches 2–3 sets of 30–60 seconds per side.

Recovery modalities (weekly)
- Self-myofascial release (SMR): 5–10 minutes total per day using a foam roller or lacrosse ball on calves, glutes, quads, IT band, and thoracic spine.
- Temperature modulation: contrast baths or contrast showers (optional, 2–3 times/week) for soreness management.
- Ice/heat as needed: ice 10–15 minutes post-workout if swelling, or heat for stiffness in non-workout days.

Breathing and core stability (3–5 minutes daily)
- Diaphragmatic breathing: 4 sets of 6 slow breaths through the nose, 4–6 seconds inhale, 6–8 seconds exhale.
- Pelvic floor engagement: 2–3 sets of 8–10 pelvic floor activation reps (Kegals) with breath.
- Talk-through bracing: 2 sets of 6–8 brisk braced breaths with a hollow abdominal cue (bracing like preparing for a punch).

Mobility circuits to perform on non-lifting days (10–15 minutes)
- Circuit A (2 rounds):
  - Hip airplanes or supported leg swings: 8 reps per side
  - 90/90 hip stretch: 30–45 seconds per side
  - Right and left hip thruster stretch with a resistance band: 30 seconds per side
  - Calf stretch with a chair: 30 seconds per side
- Circuit B (2 rounds):
  - Thoracic rotations on a foam roller: 10–12 reps per side
  - Half-kowtow stretch (kneeling hip flexor with thoracic extension): 30 seconds per side
  - Pigeon pose or modified hip opener: 30–45 seconds per side
  - Side-lying leg lifts with clamshells: 2 sets of 12–15 per side

Mobility for skiers (specific drills)
- Ankle-to-knee tracking drill: stand tall, slowly bend the knee forward over the toes while keeping the heel down; 2 sets of 10–12 reps each side.
- Lunge matrix on incline: perform step-downs and shallow lunges with a support rail to practice knee tracking through a safe ROM; 2–3 sets of 6–8 reps.

- Nutrition support: adequate protein and overall calories support tissue repair; hydration is essential.

Here is the consolidated 12-week program with all adjustments rolled in. It covers the strength plan (phases), the integrated cardio progression with higher volume in Weeks 4–8, peak weeks (9–12), the nutrition maintenance plan (including two cardio days) plus the recovery and mobility plan. It’s written as a week-by-week guide with clear sessions, exercises, sets/reps, tempo notes, and progressions. If you want, I can convert this into a printable calendar or a client-ready sheet.

Assumptions
- 36-year-old recreational lifter, post-right medial meniscus tear, cleared for low-impact strength only (no jumping, no deep knee flexion under load).
- Goal: strength and return to skiing; maintain body weight; knee-friendly ROM.
- Training site: full gym with access to barbells, dumbbells, machines, cable, and a cardio area.

Phase overview
- Phase 1: Foundations and safe tissue loading (Weeks 1–3)
- Phase 2: Strength-building with controlled knee loading (Weeks 4–8)
- Phase 3: Ski-readiness and peak strength (Weeks 9–12)

Weekly structure
- Resistance training: 4 days per week (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) with a focus on knee-friendly loading. Optional cardio on non-lift days or after workouts.
- Cardio: 2 days per week, low-to-moderate intensity; Weeks 4–8 feature increased volume and structured progression.
- Mobility and recovery: daily mobility, dedicated recovery day or finishers, and a mobility circuit 2–3 times per week.
- Nutrition: maintenance calories with protein target 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day; carbs adjusted to support training volume; fats 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day. Two cardio sessions per week integrated.

Phase 1: Foundations (Weeks 1–3)
Goal: establish form, tissue tolerance, knee-friendly strength base, rebuild mechanics.

Week 1
Day A
- Goblet Squat (or Box Squat, shallow depth): 3x10-12, tempo 3-1-1
- Romanian Deadlift (DB or Barbell): 3x8-10, tempo 2-0-2
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15 (moderate, controlled ROM to mid-range)
- Seated Leg Curl or Prone Hamstring Curl: 3x12-15
- Bulgarian Split Squat (rear foot elevated, shallow depth): 2x8-10 per leg
- Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 3x10-12
- Core: Farmer’s walk or suitcase carries 2x30s or Pallof press 2x12 each side

Day B
- Split Squat with shorter ROM (0–50 degrees): 3x8-10 per leg
- Hip Abduction/Adduction (machine): 3x12-15
- Cable pull-throughs or light Kettlebell deadlift high pull: 3x10
- Seated/Standing Calf Raise: 3x12-15
- Prone YTWL for posture: 2x8
- Mobility: 8–12 minutes (hips, quads, calves, ankle dorsiflexion)

Optional cardio: 20–25 minutes low-impact (elliptical or cycling) on off days or post-workout.

Week 2
Progression: +2–5% load where form and pain-free tolerances allow.
Day A
- Goblet Squat: 3x10-12, tempo 3-1-1
- Romanian Deadlift: 3x8-10, tempo 2-0-2
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15
- Seated Leg Curl/Prone Curl: 3x12-15
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 2x8-10 per leg (add light dumbbell if comfortable)
- Hip Thrust/Glute Bridge: 3x10-12
- Core: Anti-rotation with cable/band 2x12 per side

Optional mobility focus: 10 minutes after workouts.

Week 3
Progression: Add one more set to most exercises; or replace one exercise with a related progression if tolerable.
Day A
- Goblet Squat: 4x8-10, tempo 3-1-1
- Romanian Deadlift: 4x8
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15
- Prone/Seated Hamstring Curl: 4x10-12
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8 per leg
- Hip Thrust: 3x12
- Core: Dead Bug progressions 3x10 per side

Phase 2: Strength-building with controlled loading (Weeks 4–8)
Goal: Increase overall strength with safer ROM, hip-davor, and knee-friendly loading. Introduce more hip-dominant work and safe leg-dominant loading.

Week 4
Day A
- Front Squat or Hack Squat (shallow depth, rack-supported if needed): 3x6-8
- Romanian Deadlift or RDL with single-leg variation: 3x8-10
- Leg Press (medium depth, controlled): 3x10-12
- Leg Extension (moderate): 3x12-15
- Hip Thrust: 3x8-10
- Cable Abductor/Adductor: 2x12-15

Day B
- Split Squat (goblet or dumbbell; limit depth): 3x8 per leg
- Belted Hip Squat alternative if available: 3x8
- Glute Bridge with tempo 2-0-2: 3x10-12
- Seated Leg Curl: 3x12-15
- Calf Raise: 4x12-15
- Core: Pallof press 3x12 per side

Week 5
Day A
- Front Squat or Hack Squat: 4x6-8
- Romanian Deadlift: 4x8
- Leg Press: 3x10-12
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15
- Hip Thrust: 3x8-10
- Abductor/Adductor: 3x12-15
- Core: Bird-D-dog 3x per side

Day B
- Split Squat (dumbbell/goblet): 3x6-8 per leg
- Hip Belt Squat alternative (if available): 3x8
- Glute Bridge tempo: 3x10-12
- Seated Leg Curl: 3x12-15
- Calf Raise: 4x12-15
- Core: Anti-rotation with cable 3x12 per side

Week 6
- Pause Squats at shallow depth (box if needed): 3x5-6 with 2-second pause
- Romanian Deadlift: 4x6-8
- Leg Press or Belt Squat: 3x8-10
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15
- Hip Thrust: 4x8-10
- Lying Leg Curl: 3x12-15
- Calf Raise: 4x12-15
- Core: Dead Bug with stability ball 3x12

Week 7
Day A
- Front Squat or Box Squat: 4x6
- RDL or SLDL: 4x6-8
- Seated Leg Curl: 3x12-15
- Leg Press: 3x10-12
- Hip Thrust: 4x8-10
- Cable Hip Abduction/Adduction: 3x12-15
- Core: Anti-rotation with cable 3x12 per side

Week 8
- Increase load modestly on main lifts if form is solid.
- Front Squat or Hack Squat: 4x6-8
- Romanian Deadlift: 4x8
- Leg Press: 3x10-12
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15
- Hip Thrust: 4x8-10
- Glute Bridge variations (single-leg with light load): 3x8-10 per leg
- Calf Raise: 4x12-15
- Mobility: 10 minutes daily; increase ankle dorsiflexion work

Phase 3: Ski-readiness and higher-load strength (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Strength peak and ski-ready conditioning; heavier lifts with controlled ROM, unilateral stability, and tempo work; tapered to finish strong.

Week 9
Day A
- Back Squat (or Front Squat if comfortable; shallow depth): 4x5-6
- Romanian Deadlift: 4x6-8
- Leg Press: 3x8-10
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15
- Hip Thrust: 4x6-8
- Cable Abduction/Adduction: 3x12-15
- Core: Farmer’s carry 2x40s

Day B
- Bulgarian Split Squat (dumbbells): 3x6-8 per leg
- SLDL or RDL with tempo 3-1-1: 3x8
- Seated Leg Curl: 3x12-15
- Glute Bridge with abduction bands: 3x12
- Calf Raise: 4x12-15
- Mobility and knee-friendly warm-up: 6–8 minutes

Week 10
- Back Squat: 4x5
- Front Squat: 3x6
- Leg Press: 3x8-10
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15
- Hip Thrust: 4x8
- Nordic hamstring progressions (if safe) or glute ham raise substitute: 3x6-8
- Core: Anti-rotation with cable 3x12 per side

Week 11
- Peak preparation with tempo and speed emphasis, lower volume
- Back Squat: 3x3–5 at 85–90% 1RM; Pause Squats 3x3 at shallow depth with 2-second pause
- Romanian Deadlift: 3x4–6
- Leg Press: 3x8–10
- Leg Extension: 3x12-15
- Hip Thrust: 3x6-8
- Single-leg work: Step-ups with light load or Bulgarian Split Squat 3x6 per leg
- Calf Raise: 4x12-15
- Upper body maintenance: 3–4x4–6

Week 12
- Peak-test day and ski-readiness
- Back Squat: 3x3-5
- Front Squat: 3x4-6
- RDL/SLDL: 3x6-8
- Leg Press: 3x6-8
- Hip Thrust: 3x6-8
- Lighter accessory work to maintain movement quality: Glute bridges, leg curls, ab/adductor 2x12-15
- Conditioning finisher: 15–20 minutes of low-impact rowing or cycling at moderate intensity
- Mobility/flexibility focus: 10–15 minutes

Phase 4: Peak weeks — Recovery and ski-readiness
- Week 9–12 taper structure:
  - Volume: reduce overall weekly volume by 20–40% from Week 8 levels
  - Intensity: maintain high quality and technique; keep primary lifts above threshold
  - Frequency: 4 lifting days per week; by Week 12, sessions may be shorter with a strong emphasis on technique and movement quality
- Ski-specific drills: unilateral stability, edge control drills, proprioception on stable to unstable surfaces, and stance alignment
- Plyometrics: only after clinician clearance; if cleared, low-load, high-control plyos (no deep landings) in non-peak weeks or after clinician sign-off

Cardio plan (two days per week; Weeks 4–8 feature increased volume and progression; Weeks 9–12 taper or lower volume)
- Week 9–12: maintain 2 cardio days per week, 20–40 minutes each, but prioritize recovery and peak strength days. If fatigue accrues, reduce cardio volume by 20–30% or keep only light maintenance sessions.
- Modalities: bike, elliptical, rower, incline walking; rotate modalities to distribute knee load
- Intensity: Zone 2–3 with occasional Zone 3 blocks for short durations if knee tolerates and energy allows
- Ski-specific conditioning days (optional, low impact): light single-leg balance, edge control drills, hip hinge and core activations

Nutrition (maintenance-weight targets throughout)
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day; distribute across 4–5 meals
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg/day on higher-load weeks; 3–4 g/kg/day on lighter weeks; adjust for cardio volume
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day
- Meal timing: pre-workout meal 1.5–3 hours before training (40–60 g carbs, 15–25 g protein); post-workout 20–40 g protein + 40–60 g carbs within 1–2 hours
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day plus electrolytes on longer or hot sessions
- Supplements (optional): whey or casein protein; creatine 3–5 g/day; omega-3s; vitamin D if deficient

Recovery and mobility (daily plan)
- Daily mobility routine (5–15 minutes): ankles, hips, knee tracking, thoracic spine
- 5–10 minute warm-up before training: ankle dorsiflexion, hip hinge activation, thoracic mobility
- Daily breathing work: diaphragmatic breathing 4 sets of 6 slow breaths; braced core activation
- SMR: 5–10 minutes total per day on calves, glutes, quads, IT band, thoracic spine
- Recovery day options: active recovery (easy walk, swim, mobility), contrast showers (optional)

Knee safety and red flags
- If swelling or sharp pain increases, back off ROM, reduce intensity, or revert to Week 3–4 safety ROM
- If pain worsens with a given exercise, substitute safer variation or reduce load
- Maintain knee-friendly depth and ROM; avoid deep knee flexion under load; ensure proper valgus control during squats and lunges

Return-to-ski readiness
- Validate knee ROM and control under load with sports-specific movements (edge control, pivot-laden stance, controlled turns) without impact
- Build neuromuscular tolerance through unilateral work and tempo-focused sets
- Reintroduce plyometrics only with clinician clearance and progressive, controlled exposure

Sample weekly structure (compact example)
- Week 4, Day A: Front Squat 3x6-8; RDL 3x8-10; Leg Press 3x10-12; Leg Extension 3x12-15; Hip Thrust 3x8-10; Abductor/Adductor 2x12-15; Core 2x12
- Week 4, Day B: Split Squat e/o DBs 3x8; Glute Bridge tempo 3x10-12; Seated Leg Curl 3x12-15; Calf Raise 4x12-15; Core anti-rotation 3x12
- Week 9, Day A: Back Squat 4x4-5; RDL 4x6; Leg Press 3x8; Hip Thrust 4x6-8; Core 2–3 sets
- Week 9, Day B: Bulgarian Split Squat 3x6-8 per leg; SLDL 3x6; Seated Leg Curl 3x12; Calf Raise 4x12
- Week 12, Day A: Squat top sets + lighter accessory for technique; 1RM testing or top set with close monitoring
- Week 12, Day B: Ski-specific drills and mobility; optional light cardio
